text: Good morning, this is Send7 World News in 7 Minutes. I'm Stephen Devincenzi. Today is Tuesday the 16th of July 2024.
Starting in the Americas today, in the United States, both President Joe Biden and former
President Donald Trump have called for calm and unity following the assassination attempt
on Trump on Saturday. Biden has ordered a review of how it was possible for the attacker to get
close enough to shoot Trump. Speaking from the White House, Biden said that the U.S. cannot go down
the path of political violence. A former president was shot, an American citizen killed, while simply
exercising his freedom to support the candidate of his choosing. We cannot, we must not go down this
road in America. We've traveled before throughout our history. Violence has never been the answer.
Former President Trump announced yesterday that his choice for vice president is J.D. Vance,
a senator from Ohio. Argentina has won the Copa America football tournament, beating Colombia 1-0
in the final in the U.S. city of Miami. Argentina has won the Copa America 16 times, more than any other
team. In Brazil, the model and Instagram influencer Cat Torres has been sentenced to eight years in jail
for human trafficking and slavery. Over 20 women say that Torres scammed or exploited them, with some
saying that they were trafficked to the United States and forced to work. A judge gave Torres the eight-year
sentence for crimes relating to just one of Torres' followers, who the judge said was taken abroad for
sexual exploitation. Africa. In Somalia, a car bomb has killed five people in the capital Mogadishu.
The Islamist jihadist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. In Rwanda, there were presidential
elections yesterday, although elections in Rwanda are generally not considered to be free and fair by
international observers. Paul Kagame has been president of Rwanda since the year 2000, but has
effectively ruled Rwanda since 1994. There were two other candidates in this election, however many other
opposition candidates were not allowed to run. Asia and Oceania. Pakistan's government is planning to ban
the political party of former Prime Minister Imran Khan, according to Information Minister Atala Tara.
Khan's party, Teriq-e-Insaf, won the most seats in parliament in the last two elections. However, Tara said
yesterday that the party would be banned because of proven charges of Teriq-e-Insaf receiving foreign money
and because of the rioting of its supporters. In New Zealand, the rarest whale in the world has been
found washed up on a beach. Spade-toothed whales are famous for the fact that they have never been seen
alive, and scientists don't know how many there are, what they eat, or where they live. New Zealand's
conservation agency said that finding this spade-toothed whale could help to discover a lot of new
information about the species. Europe. Estonian Prime Minister Kaya Kallas has announced her resignation
in order to take the position of European Union Foreign Policy Chief, currently held by Josep Borrell.
Kallas has been Prime Minister of Estonia for three and a half years, and is well known for her strong
stance against Russia and in support of Ukraine. She will remain as Prime Minister until a new government
is formed. In Italy, a pilot programme in Venice which charged people 5 euros for a day visit to Venice
has finished. Over 2 million euros was raised from the fee, however opposition politicians have said that
the fee did not work, as the number of people visiting during this period was more than in previous years,
showing that people were not dissuaded from visiting. Venice tourism officials have suggested that the
entry fee may return next year, and could be raised to 10 euros. In Ukraine, the Ukrainian army is making
small advances in the Russian-occupied parts of Kharkiv region, and has recaptured one village and some
parts of the city of Vovchansk over the last few days. In Donetsk region, the Russian army is continuing to
make small advances, and has claimed to take control of one village. Ukraine has said that Russia has
removed its last navy ship from the occupied region of Crimea. Crimea officially holds the headquarters
of Russia's Black Sea fleet, however, Ukraine's repeated successful strikes on ships and submarines in
Sevastopol port have forced Russia to move them away from Crimea. And studies in Sweden and Denmark have
suggested that the Neolithic population decline may have been caused by plague. The Neolithic decline was a
fast drop in the human population between 5,000 and 6,000 years ago, and came shortly after a fast
increase of the human population when humans first practised agriculture. Researchers in Sweden and Denmark have
studied the DNA from bones and teeth, and found that 32% of them were infected with plague, a similar plague to the
black death which killed half of Europe's population in the 14th century. Today, cases and deaths from plague are
extremely rare. That's your world news in seven minutes. If you enjoy this podcast, please tell someone about it.
You can get in touch with us by sending an email to podcast at send7.org. We do read every message.
Have a great day. See you tomorrow.
